purpose: R260 bounded soft-freshness penalty on R257 versus the matched R257 control

universe.industry_source: current ext_hy_ths industry snapshot; not historical PIT

factor.formula: quality_rs_soft_fresh_rank = rank_pct(quality_relative_strength_min_rank) * (1 - 0.20 * prior20_r257_top30_count / 20) within historical nonfinancial HS300 members
factor.pit_rule: Prior R257 Top30 counts use only the preceding 20 benchmark trading dates; current ranks use same-date eligible historical nonfinancial HS300 members

pit_audit.rule: rank_pct(R257) multiplied by a bounded recency penalty based on prior R257 Top30 count within historical nonfinancial HS300 members; R257 value required
pit_audit.rank_normalization: rank_pct = (number_of_names - descending_average_rank) / (number_of_names - 1); 1 is best and 0 is worst

samples.rolling_1y: 252-trading-day rolling compounded return over the stitched 2023-2026 curve
samples.recent_12m: last 252 trading-day returns of the stitched 2023-2026 curve

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four components proportionally
execution.stitching: two segment returns compounded into one curve; first day of each later segment skipped

caveats: The soft-freshness design is a result-driven follow-up to R257/R258/R259 and is not independent confirmation.
The 20-day recency count depends on strict Top30 tie-breaking and complete benchmark dates.
A 20% maximum haircut may be too gentle to change concentration.
R253 and industry-relative strength were researched in overlapping samples, so multiple-comparison risk remains.
The industry snapshot used to exclude financials is current rather than historical PIT.
Financial values inherit provider restatement and publication-timing risk.
The full curve is stitched from two system-engine segments; segment boundaries can reset an open position.
Trade P&L shares are contribution diagnostics from two segments each starting at 1,000,000 notional.
Passing every gate would justify paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
